item.title: Meet Bartlomiej Kubkowski: The first man to swim 100 miles across the Baltic Sea from Sweden to Poland
item.description: In a remarkable display of endurance, Bartlomiej Kubkowski swam an astonishing 160 kilometers continuously across the Baltic Sea, achieving this incredible milestone in 55 hours and 10 minutes. After four previous attempts without success, his persistence finally bore fruit, helping to raise nearly $190,000 for children battling cancer. This achievement signifies a noteworthy moment in the annals of marathon swimming history.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Los Angeles singer taught her rescue horse to play the guitar and harp
item.description: In a fascinating blend of music and animal companionship, a California singer-songwriter is working on a groundbreaking album alongside her rescue horse, Yupia. Using his nose and teeth, Yupia has mastered playing the guitar and harp, creating a partnership that has captivated millions online. The album promises a heartwarming fusion of Yupia's unique sounds and Khramov's vocal artistry, showcasing the profound trust and bond formed between humans and animals.

item.title: Scientists tested road dust in 7 eastern US cities; toxic legacy metals linger near parks, schools
item.description: In seven eastern cities of the U.S., road dust harbors toxic metals linked to historical industrial actions. These contaminants remain entrenched, presenting health dangers through regular dust interactions, especially for children who are more susceptible due to their behaviors and smaller size. Areas in the Northeast exhibit higher concentrations of these metals, a reflection of their extended industrial past. Recognizing these enduring pollutants is vital for effective community health strategies.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Surviving NYC on $35K: Woman shares the budget blueprint
item.description: A New Yorker named Julia lives in Brooklyn on $35,000 annually after taxes. She shares an apartment, paying $1,200 monthly for rent, which is a significant expense. Julia strategically shops at Trader Joe's and Aldi for groceries, spending $250 each month. Her transportation costs are kept low at $70 monthly using a Fair Fares OMNY card. Entertainment and fitness are managed through free apps and affordable dance classes.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: In 2023, a veterinarian left a $150,000 job; three years later, relief work pays twice as much
item.description: Oregon veterinarian Ron Titterington made a bold move, leaving his lucrative executive position for flexible relief shifts. Surprisingly, he now earns double his previous salary while achieving a healthier work-life balance. This shift highlights the increasing trend of seasoned veterinarians prioritizing well-being over traditional burnout, as the high demand for relief vets significantly enriches their earnings. Titterington plans to pursue this gratifying path rather than opting for full retirement.

item.title: TikTok Star Enters Hospice: Family say Sydney Towle is in end-of-life care; fans recall Miami runway
item.description: TikTok creator Sydney Towle, 26, has entered hospice care after a three-year battle with the rare bile duct cancer cholangiocarcinoma. Her family shared the emotional update, thanking supporters for their love and prayers. Diagnosed at 23, Towle inspired more than 1.1 million followers by documenting her journey with honesty, hope, and resilience. Despite her worsening condition, she remained optimistic, reminding fans that miracles can happen and encouraging others to never lose hope.
item.dc:creator: Global Sports Desk

item.title: Who is Sadhana Gollapudi? Row over Indian woman's dancing video as she's baselessly accused of visa fraud; US attorney says she's a naturalized citizen
item.description: An Indian-American woman's online life took a dark turn when she was falsely accused of visa fraud. A hate account shared Sadhana Gollapudi's dancing video and claimed that she had been on a student visa since 2014. A US attorney stepped in, clarifying her status as a naturalized citizen. The entire episode triggered a massive row and Gollapudi too issued a statement.

item.title: In 1986, Australia eradicated rabbits from an island stripped bare by 150 years of grazing
item.description: Phillip Island has undergone a remarkable environmental turnaround following an extensive pest eradication initiative. The island is witnessing a resurgence of native flora and is nurturing thriving colonies of migratory seabirds. Each year, it becomes a safe haven for thousands of seabirds to breed. Ongoing restoration efforts aim to safeguard native wildlife and reinforce vulnerable soil ecosystems, making it a crucial sanctuary for reptiles that have vanished from other regions.

item.title: Chicago study links more urban tree cover to fewer deaths
item.description: A new study by Northwestern University has found that neighbourhoods in Chicago that lost more tree canopy over 11 years also recorded higher mortality rates, particularly in hotter areas. The researchers say protecting mature trees, along with planting new ones, could help reduce heat-related health risks and improve public health in cities.

item.title: Why New York turned 5,000 discarded toilets into oyster reefs beneath Jamaica Bay
item.description: New York City repurposed nearly five thousand old toilets into artificial reef structures. These porcelain fixtures now provide a base for juvenile oyster growth in Jamaica Bay. Oyster reefs are vital for filtering pollutants and improving water quality in New York Harbour. Decades of pollution and overfishing had previously destroyed these important natural systems. This initiative supports broader coastal resilience and habitat restoration efforts across the region.
